source_text.lib/letflow/design/req237-zig-provenance: ss2 defines the marker text (fixed literal: `PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):`) and the placement rule with FOUR citation-unit shapes as of the 2026-09-05 ISS-0510 amendment: (1) single citation line -- insert the marker on its own line immediately above a SOURCE:/CONTRACT SOURCE:-style line or lone bullet (and any hard-wrapped continuation lines of the same sentence); (2) paragraph -- for a .zig filename embedded in prose, the marker precedes the WHOLE paragraph (bounded by blank lines), not just the sentence/token; (3) table -- one marker above the table's header row, never per-row; (4) YAML comment-line/sequence-item (ISS-0510 addition) -- when the citation unit lives inside a YAML file and the enclosing context is itself a YAML comment, or a plain scalar/sequence item that cannot take a bare non-comment text line immediately above it without corrupting YAML syntax, the marker is inserted as a `# `-prefixed YAML comment line containing the identical marker text verbatim, immediately above the unit. Two sub-cases: (a) a bare #-prefixed comment line immediately above a single sequence-item bullet, or above an id:/title: key pair whose value contains the citation (marker precedes title: when id:+title: are treated as one requirement-entry unit); (b) when the citation is itself inside a commented-out `# ---`-delimited section-header block, the marker precedes the whole block as one unit, not per header line. De-duplication: if a marker already immediately precedes a unit (grep -B1 check), do not insert a second one -- this makes the rule idempotent. ss2(a) gives the exact regex: `PROVENANCE \(historical, not current decision authority\):` (also matches with plain `grep -F`). ss4 gives two worked before/after examples (docs/requirements.yaml SOURCE: line, and an inline-prose moduledoc paragraph) showing the original path text is preserved byte-identical, only one new line added. ss5 gives the verification method: (i) total-marked-count grep before/after must increase by exactly the number of citation units marked; (ii) `grep -c '\.zig' <file>` before/after must be EQUAL per file (no path text lost); (iii) idempotency -- re-running the pass a second time produces zero new markers. docs/issues/*.yaml is YAML, so shape (4) may well apply here wherever a .zig citation sits inside a commented-out block, a sequence-item bullet, or a scalar key/value that cannot take a bare prose line directly above it without corrupting YAML syntax -- apply shape (4)'s sub-cases exactly as documented for docs/requirements.yaml. REQ-260 (sibling chunk 239f, same docs/issues/*.yaml family) already found and applied a mechanical extension of shape 4(a) to r_co_evidence:/letflow_evidence: YAML sequences (each .zig-carrying quoted string item individually marked with its own '#'-prefixed comment line immediately above it) -- ISS-0085.yaml (spot-read at Step 00) uses the equivalent `r_co_sources:` sequence, so expect the same pattern to apply here. If a genuinely new citation-unit shape is found that does not match ANY of the four documented shapes (or REQ-260's already-established r_co_evidence:/r_co_sources:-sequence extension of shape 4a), do NOT invent a fifth ad-hoc convention: flag it as a new issue for CODE-DESIGNER (the same process ISS-0510 was raised through -- describe the shape, cite the file/line, and note it in this handoff's result.issues at MAJOR or MINOR per your judgement of how many citations it affects) and apply the CLOSEST-MATCHING existing shape in the meantime with a clear note in your result.summary.
